definitions: A cognitive bias in which consumers tend to have a specific change in preference between two options when also presented with a third option that is asymmetrically dominated.
A phenomenon in marketing where the introduction of a third, less attractive option makes one of the original two options seem more appealing.
examples: The company used the decoy effect to boost sales of its premium product.
Understanding the decoy effect is crucial for pricing strategies.
The experiment demonstrated a clear decoy effect among participants.
